Génocide : les dessous d’un mot puissant: Genocide: The Underpinnings of a Powerful and Complex Word
« À l’intention de détruire, en tout ou: “With intent to destroy, in whole or in part, a national, ethnical, racial or religious group”
Sur les réseaux sociaux comme sur le res: On social media and across the rest of the web, in Canada and elsewhere in the world, many dignitaries, researchers, organizations and members of civil society are describing the Israeli attacks launched since October 8 as a prelude to “genocide.” This is sparking heated debate in the public sphere and among the political class. Yet in Western media, some specialists are calling for the term not to be used for now. Even so, the massacres under way in Gaza are labelled “genocide” every day. The term seems to linger in people’s minds. How can this paradox be explained? And is a genocide unfolding before our eyes right now?
D’autre part, quand peut-on faire appel: Meanwhile, when can this legal concept be invoked, and what are its limits? La Converse turned to experts to untangle the threads of an issue with complex ramifications.
<strong>Qui parle de génocide et pourquo: Who is talking about genocide, and why?
À Gaza, plusieurs journalistes locaux do: In Gaza, several local journalists have been documenting the fate of their people every day since the Hamas attacks in Israel. Between power outages and the impossibility of getting regular access to the Internet, their reports show the rest of the world the hell into which this small strip of land has been plunged since October 8. Relentless bombings, shortages of water and food, limited or even nonexistent health care and emergency services, forced displacement, decimated families… fear and insecurity lurk everywhere.
Le 21 novembre, 5 journalistes palestini: On November 21, five Palestinian journalists relayed a message signed by their colleague Yara Eid on Instagram. <l1>Backed by videos</l1>, she made an impassioned plea: “Gaza is still being wiped out. [...] We need you to call for a permanent ceasefire. We still need you to call for an end to this genocide.”
Au même moment, côté israélien, plusieur: At the same time, on the Israeli side, several elected officials have publicly made dehumanizing remarks about Palestinians and welcomed the fate awaiting them. “We are fighting human animals,” Israeli Defence Minister Yoav Gallant declared, for example, on October 9. A few days later, Ghassan Alian, a senior Netanyahu general, used the same expression and added a promise of <l1>“destruction” and “hell.”</l1>
Le 28 octobre, le média Mekomit révélait: On October 28, the outlet Mekomit revealed the contents of an Israeli Intelligence Ministry document recommending <l1>the forced transfer of Gaza’s 2.2 million residents to Mount Sinai</l1>, in Egypt, reviving fears of ethnic cleansing among many observers.
Pour les journalistes de Gaza et nombre: For Gaza’s journalists and many human rights defenders, these statements and revelations leave no doubt that the ongoing attacks amount to genocide.
Du côté des manifestants qui se réunisse: Among the demonstrators who have gathered every week since the start of the Israeli assault, Yara Eid’s words are taken up and chanted loud and clear. In Montréal, the signs and chants repeat the same thing: “A ceasefire now! End the genocide immediately!”
Parmi la foule montréalaise, nous croiso: In the Montréal crowd, we meet Rama El-Malah, who is of Palestinian origin. She is one of the organizers of the Palestinian Youth Movement (PYM). The student has been living the attacks targeting her people intensely for more than a month. “It’s been very hard, that’s for sure. I think every member of the community can attest to that. Everyone deals with it in their own way. Some people are in mourning, especially those who have family in Gaza… That’s a completely normal reaction. Others have kept organizing.”
Elle s’inquiète du sort des Palestiniens: She worries about the fate of Palestinians throughout the occupied territories, as a rise in attacks on civilians in the West Bank is also being recorded. “All eyes are on Gaza, but that goes without saying because of the genocide taking place there right now.”
Aux quatre coins du monde, d’autres voix: All over the world, other voices are speaking out about an imminent or ongoing genocide in Gaza. Among them are more than 800 scholars and practitioners of international law and conflict and genocide studies, who signed <l1>a collective statement</l1> on October 15 to sound the alarm, saying they fear a genocide is under way in Gaza.
À leur suite, les Nations unies évoquent: Following them, the United Nations spoke of “a risk of genocide in Gaza” on November 2. UN experts expressed concern about serious violations committed against Palestinians. These are “a reinforcement of the incitement to genocide,” <l1>according to this group of experts</l1>.
À Paris, deux mois après le début des at: In Paris, two months after the start of the attacks on Gaza, the International Federation for Human Rights (FIDH) adopted a resolution recognizing the “ongoing genocide” of the Palestinian people and urging the international community to do everything possible to stop it.
Plusieurs semaines auparavant, l’avocat: Several weeks earlier, human rights lawyer Craig Mokhiber had resigned with a bang from his post as director of the New York office of the United Nations Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights to signal his dismay at the UN’s inaction. In his view, the situation in Gaza is <l1>“a textbook case of genocide.”</l1>
Dans sa lettre, M. Mokhiber – qui a égal: In his letter, Mr. Mokhiber, who has also worked on the genocides suffered by the Tutsis, the Yazidis, Bosnian Muslims and the Rohingya, writes that “the current wholesale slaughter of the Palestinian people, rooted in an ethno-nationalist settler-colonial ideology, in continuity of decades of their systematic persecution and purging, based entirely upon their status as Arabs, and coupled with explicit statements of intent by leaders in the Israeli government and military, leaves no room for doubt or debate.”
L’avocat interpelle les grandes puissanc: The lawyer calls out the major Western powers, which “facilitate the genocide” by supporting Israel economically and militarily, and by refusing to ensure respect for the Geneva Conventions. He also accuses those countries’ corporate media of being complicit in the continual dehumanization of the Palestinian people, and of spreading “propaganda for war and advocacy of national, racial or religious hatred.”
Cette sortie publique pour sonner l’alar: This public statement sounding the alarm over what many consider to be a genocide in Gaza joins that of <l1>several Jewish voices</l1>, including <l2>Gabor Maté</l2>, a Canadian whose parents are Holocaust survivors. The author and physician admits he has “never seen such atrocities, committed in plain view on TV, with the victims presented as the aggressor.”
Le mot génocide relève d’abord et avant: The word genocide first and foremost belongs to a legal framework: international law. The term is defined in the <l1>Convention on the Prevention and Punishment of the Crime of Genocide</l1>, drafted in 1946. It refers to “intent to destroy, in whole or in part, a national, ethnical, racial or religious group,” by means of any one of these five acts:
a) Meurtre de membres du groupe: a) Killing members of the group
b) Atteinte grave à l’intégrité physique: b) Causing serious bodily or mental harm to members of the group
c) Soumission intentionnelle du groupe à: c) Deliberately inflicting on the group conditions of life calculated to bring about its physical destruction in whole or in part
d) Mesures visant à entraver les naissan: d) Imposing measures intended to prevent births within the group
e) Transfert forcé d’enfants du groupe à: e) Forcibly transferring children of the group to another group
Pour qu’un événement de violence de mass: For an event of mass violence to be officially recognized as such, a court must hand down a verdict finding that genocide occurred. The only bodies authorized to try this type of crime are the International Criminal Court (ICC), certain national courts of ICC member countries, and the international tribunals established following UN resolutions. Most often, justice is rendered several years after the events: in the case of the former Yugoslavia, the decision came in 2004, nine years after the massacres.
Pour les juristes appelés à statuer sur: For the jurists called on to rule on a possible genocide, the main difficulty lies in establishing intent. It is this special intent that distinguishes the crime of genocide from other international crimes.
Pour ce qui est de la situation prévalan: As for the situation currently prevailing in the Israeli-Palestinian zone, the ICC’s chief prosecutor, Karim Khan, recently travelled to Israel and Ramallah. On December 3, he said his office was documenting the Israeli and Hamas attacks in order to investigate possible <l1>war crimes and crimes against humanity</l1>, even though Israel is not a member of the ICC, unlike the Palestinian Authority. For now, the ICC has not indicated that it intends to take steps to investigate allegations of genocide in Palestine.
Selon le professeur A. Dirk Moses, histo: According to Professor A. Dirk Moses, a historian specializing in genocide studies and editor of the Journal of Genocide, the very definition of the term “genocide” is restrictive, which makes it difficult to use before international courts.
En effet, aux yeux du droit internationa: Indeed, in the eyes of international law, and as we said above, genocide occurs when any one of the listed acts is “committed with intent to destroy, in whole or in part, a national, ethnical, racial or religious group, as such.” For the professor, the words “as such” narrow the scope of application and interpretation of events of mass violence.
« Pour dire que l’on est face à un génoc: “To say that we are facing a genocide, you have to prove that one of the targeted acts was committed against members of a group solely because they are members of a group.” States can therefore claim that they attacked members of that group not because they belong to it, but because they were suspected of taking part in an insurgency.
Selon lui, il est donc très facile pour: In his view, it is therefore very easy for states to deny the genocidal nature of their attacks: “They claim that their behaviour is driven by a military or security logic of victory, rather than a destructive logic of genocide.”
Le caractère restrictif du terme exister: The term’s restrictive nature exists by design, to protect states’ sovereignty vis-à-vis the Convention, the researcher explains. In his view, the first signatory states knowingly built a loophole into the framework defining genocide so they could resort to violence and defend their interests with impunity.
« Les États [...] veulent être en mesure: “States [...] want to be able to wage the kind of war the Israelis are waging today, or that the Americans waged in Korea in the 1950s and in Vietnam in the 1960s and 1970s, or the Russians in Chechnya in the 1990s. [...] In other words, violent attacks on the civilian population in the context of a civil war.”
Dans ce contexte, quel poids ont les voi: In this context, how much weight do the voices denouncing an ongoing genocide and pointing the finger at the Hebrew state and its allies carry, such as that of Colombian President Gustavo Petro or, closer to home, that of Ontario MPP <l1>Sarah Jama</l1>? Are their fears well founded?
De l’avis de l’historien, les pouvoirs o: In the historian’s view, Western powers are unlikely to line up behind the supporters of the Palestinian cause who denounce a genocide. After all, he points out, the legal concept of genocide was modelled on the atrocities committed during the Holocaust, and the memory of that event remains strong. The symbolic weight of the past therefore tips the scales heavily. “In a way, Jews are the ultimate victims of genocide. So they can’t be the perpetrators of an event similar to the Holocaust.”
Malgré cette conjoncture particulière, M: Despite this particular situation, Mr. Moses notes that this difficulty in obtaining recognition is most often the lot of peoples of the Global South. By contrast, media attention and popular support in the West quickly focused on the war in Ukraine. Two months after the start of hostilities, in February 2021, <l1>U.S. President Joe Biden used the term to describe the Russian invasion of Ukraine. Prime Minister Justin Trudeau later expressed concern that the escalating violence was “looking more and more like genocide.”</l1>
Rappelons que la CPI a émis en mars dern: It bears recalling that in March, the ICC issued an arrest warrant against Russian President Vladimir Putin for war crimes, only two weeks after the ICC chief prosecutor’s office announced it was opening a file to investigate allegations of war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide.
Tout cela illustre l’aspect colonial et: All of this illustrates the colonial and racial aspect of the concept, the professor believes. He cites the <l1>war in Biafra</l1> (1967–1970), which killed more than 3 million people. At the time, a solidarity movement called for an “end to the genocide.” But the systematic rape of women, the deaths of thousands, and the deliberate use of a siege to deprive Biafra’s civilian populations of water and food were not factors taken into account in describing these atrocities as genocide, either at the time or to this day.
Le génocide apparaît ainsi comme « le cr: Genocide thus appears as “the international crime par excellence.” But the bar is high for horror to be labelled as such.
« Pour les peuples colonisés, il est dif: “For colonized peoples, it is difficult to claim that they are victims of destruction. It is obviously a powerful concept for victim groups because it is considered the crime of crimes in international law, and if you can argue successfully, if you can convince people that you are the victim of a genocidal campaign, then you get recognition and, perhaps, intervention.”
Devant ce dédale politique, M. Moses s’i: Faced with this political maze, Mr. Moses questions the ranking of the various international crimes: it is “grotesque” that these categorizations mean countless tragedies occur without being given much attention. Regardless of which group it is directed at, “mass violence should provoke an outcry strong enough to be at the heart of international actors’ concerns and to be stopped by a swift and appropriate response.”
Au lendemain des attaques perpétrées par: In the aftermath of the attacks carried out by Hamas on October 7, most major Western media focused exclusively on condemning Hamas. However, many criticized <l1>the lack of historical context for understanding the root causes</l1> of this traumatic event for Israel, which was also the trigger for a series of massacres in the Gaza territory.
Selon Michaël Séguin, professeur adjoint: According to Michaël Séguin, an assistant professor at Saint Paul University and a sociologist of ethnic relations by training, the history of the Israeli-Palestinian conflict is part of a process of settler colonialism. These decades of repeated attacks in the Gaza Strip against a backdrop of occupation by the Hebrew state, he says, bear all the hallmarks of a genocidal process. The Israeli assault would be merely the tip of an iceberg submerged in time.
À la fin du 19<sup>e</sup> siècle et au: In the late 19<sup>th</sup> and early 20<sup>th</sup> centuries, the architects of political Zionism allied themselves with major Western powers, notably Great Britain (1917). Thus, despite the Holocaust and the tragic persecution of Jews in Europe, “the State of Israel is a construction sponsored by Westerners, which rests on the gradual appropriation of Palestinian lands,” the professor points out.
Avant l’arrivée de colons juifs européen: Before the arrival of European Jewish settlers, a relative harmony existed under the Ottoman Empire between the Christian and Muslim communities living in Palestine alongside Jews. Under <l1>the British Mandate (1920–1948)</l1>, the process of seizing territory intensified and culminated in 1947 with <l2>the unfair partition of historic Palestinian territory</l2>.
L’année 1948 marque la création de l’Éta: The year 1948 marked the creation of the State of Israel and a turning point in relations between the two peoples. “In the war that followed, which Israelis call the War of Independence and Palestinians call al-Nakba (the catastrophe), 750,000 Palestinians became refugees and 500 of their villages were destroyed by the new state. Today, three-quarters of Gaza’s residents are themselves refugees and descendants of refugees from the 1948 ethnic cleansing campaign,” Mr. Séguin explains.
Au lendemain de la Nakba, Israël détient: In the aftermath of the Nakba, Israel held 78% of Palestinian territory. It left only the enclaves of the West Bank, East Jerusalem and Gaza under Arab control. In 1967, Israel continued its expansion into those territories.
En 2002, le jeune État entame l’édificat: In 2002, the young state began building a wall between itself and the West Bank, which activists for the Palestinian cause call an “apartheid wall.” Several Israeli settlements went up along the wall, at the expense of Palestinian farmers who were dispossessed of their agricultural land. Starting in 2007, in reaction to Hamas’s election, Israel began its siege of the Gaza Strip: controlling the comings and goings of Palestinian civilians and monitoring airways and access to the sea.
Selon un rapport d’Amnistie internationa: According to a 2022 Amnesty International report, this situation amounts to <l1>a regime of apartheid.</l1> “In this context, it is inevitable that resistance emerges, and most of the time it is relatively peaceful, <l2>as we saw during the peaceful Fridays of the Great March of Return</l2>. But sometimes, this resistance periodically takes armed forms, with all the tragedy that entails for those who fall victim to it,” Mr. Séguin says.
Mais qu’en est-il des accusations de gén: But what about the accusations of genocide in Gaza against Israel? “Settler colonialism rests on a process of erasing the presence of Indigenous peoples in order to establish a colonizing people in their place (...). <l1>It rests on a genocidal process</l1>, and I’m not making that up, it’s documented*. In Israel-Palestine we’re in the long term: we’re facing a process of population replacement that leads to ethnic cleansing and, ultimately, to genocide,” Mr. Séguin continues.
Cela n’indique pas forcément que l’on so: This does not necessarily mean we are facing a government that long ago planned the immediate disappearance of the 2.2 million Gazans living on a territory the size of the island of Montréal, the researcher qualifies, however.
Sur la scène internationale, il serait s: On the international stage, it would be surprising if countries like Australia, the United States or Canada, all of which have a colonial history and are regularly accused of being genocidal powers toward the Indigenous populations living within their borders, chose to adopt a position that goes against Israel’s interests.
La solidarité entre Israël et le Canada: Solidarity between Israel and Canada is nothing new, and the country has been multiplying economic partnerships and displays of alliance with Israel since the start of the Justin Trudeau era, Mr. Séguin points out. “Canada doesn’t have a veto at the UN, but for at least a good twenty years, every time there is a motion condemning Israel’s occupation and colonization, Canada systematically opposes anything that could be an explicit condemnation of Israel, even more than the United States does.”
Dans une déclaration conjointe avec les: In a joint statement with the leaders of New Zealand and Australia dated December 11, however, the Canadian prime minister did an about-face, declaring that he was aligning himself with members of the international community and calling for a permanent ceasefire. Canada had previously argued in favour of humanitarian pauses.
Les échos qui nous parviennent de Gaza r: The echoes reaching us from Gaza resonate in a particular way for survivors of mass violence, war crimes and genocides.
C’est le cas de Pierre*, un survivant du: That is the case for Pierre*, a survivor of the Rwandan genocide who has been living in Canada for several years. With an affable face, a calm voice and a philosophical tone born of necessity, the speaker has shared his story more than once to honour his promise to nurture the duty of remembrance.
Obtenir la reconnaissance d’un génocide,: Getting a genocide recognized means becoming David and going up against Goliath, Pierre explains. Having closely followed the developments leading to the prosecution of the accomplices and those responsible for the atrocities committed in Rwanda in 1994, he recalls how those court proceedings were a series of roller-coaster ups and downs punctuated by frustration.
« Qu’on parle de génocide ou de crimes d: “Whether we’re talking about genocide or war crimes, (...) the law is political. It’s a minefield. Powers like the United States or the United Kingdom won’t point the finger at another state if it doesn’t serve their interests. If it does, they’ll devote resources and use their influence to make it happen.”
Il évoque aussi la difficulté de monter: He also mentions how difficult it is to build a case to prove genocide before a court. “In Rwanda’s case, the facts were crystal clear, but they were met with a hard line, and we still had to go through the whole process. There is very little consensus on this.”
Au sujet de la situation qui prévaut act: On the situation currently unfolding in the Israeli-Palestinian territory, he wants to make one thing clear: “As a survivor of a genocide, of course I have a great deal of compassion for the Jewish people and for what they have endured as a people. Antisemitism has existed for centuries, and it is still present in our societies. But the line between victim and aggressor is thin, and change in history is possible.”
Même s’il considère qu’il est vain de mo: Even though he considers it futile to use the word “genocide” because of its heavy political charge, Pierre believes it is necessary to sound the alarm to prevent the loss of human lives. “I think people are right to demand a ceasefire. I condemn Israel’s actions in the strongest possible terms. What is happening before our eyes is a disproportionate response to the anger of a nation that was humiliated in the first place.”
« J’espère que la paix prévaudra et que: “I hope peace will prevail and the guns will fall silent,” he concludes.
L’hécatombe des deux derniers mois est s: The carnage of the past two months is unprecedented in the history of the conflict. At the time of writing, according to information reported by the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs, nearly 1.9 million people have been displaced and nearly 18,000 civilians have been killed in Gaza, which surpasses the figures of the Nakba. The number of civilian victims on the Israeli side, for its part, has been revised downward to 1,200 deaths. Roughly 135 hostages <l1>remain captive</l1> following the Hamas attack of October 7.
